script: Respect time off and don't 'stress' you on your days off? Sure. Works both ways.. I don't work for the best company. It's corporate, and the higher-ups have zero clue what goes down at ground level. When I started, a solid manager kept us from all the political crap that usually drags down a store. He got promoted out of the shop, and after a few misfires we got a new manager. Loud as a megaphone, she'd drop controversial opinions in the middle of chats with friends and swear like a sailor. Some customers would quietly ask me why I hadn't reported her, then roll their eyes when I said, "She's my manager." (I know, right?) We have a system for who to call if the manager's not there. It's a tiny crew, so we each work solo. If the manager is coming in the morning, we ping her the night before with concerns. If she's not, we hit up the assistant. Simple. I spotted a food‑health code violation from one of our vendors, snapped a pic, and texted her immediately. I wrote: "I need you guys to understand that if the store is not on fire, your not being robbed your need to be contacting (assistant manager's name) not me unless its an emergency please." (literally insane) Four days later she texts me, scolding me for "not doing my job," then a few minutes later says, "Oh, you DID do it. Sorry." She also throws in some points from our store's "good job" system. I didn't reply—because I wasn't on the clock. Then she asks me for my pay rate for a review. I answered, even though it's technically her job to know that. After that, I started getting texts like, "Do you know where the scissors went?" and other random stuff that, according to the precedent she set, isn't a store emergency and isn't my problem unless I am on the clock. I decided: no more answering unless I am on the clock. She calls; I let voicemail. She texts; I read but don't respond. The company just rolled out a "no phones while on the clock" policy, so she can't text or call me during hours unless she uses the store phone. (And honestly?) They also want us to use a mandatory app for store communication, but the policy says no phones at work. I asked on the welcome message of the new app whether they're lifting the phone ban or expecting us to work off‑clock. Everyone in the company saw my question, and the answer was just "we'll get back to you," which still hasn't happened—now nobody's using the app because the policy says we can't laugh out loud. Guess she'll have to show up in person on her days off if she wants to talk to me. Maybe she shouldn't have chewed my ass out so hard when I just sent her 1 text…
